## The structural taxonomy (pick ONE category for the change you build)
- **pretext**: a new pretext task / training objective (a new prediction target, a new self-supervised task, a new loss on new targets -- not a re-weighting of the existing losses)
- **data**: the data source, curation or tiling (which tiles are trained on, how they are drawn, re-tiled at another size or magnification, filtered or balanced by a computed signal; the data bank builds new datasets)
- **architecture**: an architecture component (a new module, token type, attention pattern or branch; may be randomly initialised)
- **schedule**: the training-schedule STRUCTURE (multi-stage training, a curriculum over views / resolution / difficulty, redistributing the fixed compute across the run -- not an LR / warmup / decay value)
- **context**: slide / spatial context (neighbouring tiles, several tiles of one slide as one sample, multi-instance objectives, position within the slide)
- **pathology**: pathology-specific structure (stain physics and stain variation, magnification, cell / nucleus / tissue relations, morphology)

OUT OF SCOPE for this lane (rejected at intake as `bold_knob_only`): a knob / weight / temperature / ratio change of
an existing term, a learning-rate / warmup / decay / layer-decay schedule value, switching an existing option on or
off, re-weighting the existing losses. Judged on the diff (only config values or constants of existing code
changed) and by an independent judge. Retuning comes AFTER: a promising bold node gets up to 5 tuning trials of
its own before its mechanism is judged.

MAKE IT TUNABLE (rejected at finish / intake as `untunable_moonshot`): the loop tunes every structural change BEFORE it
is judged (up to 5 trials, steered by your diagnostic: engaged-but-negative tries lower doses first, not-engaged tries
higher ones, reversed flips the direction where the knob is signed; a new backbone / init also gets an lr x layer-decay
grid and a warmup child). So expose the strength of what you build as numeric config keys with the current value as
default (a loss weight, a mask / drop ratio, a temperature, a dropout, a number of tokens). If the diff adds no
numeric config key and is not a backbone / init swap, declare `components` in finish -- [{family, mechanism, share,
target, knobs: [{key, lo, hi, scale}]}] -- naming the existing or new config keys the ladder may move. A structural
node is not closed as negative before >= 3 tuned points exist (unless its first point is catastrophic with the
mechanism engaged), so a first run at an untuned dose is a draft, not a verdict.

## How to arrive at the idea
Start from what the recipe structurally lacks for pathology at this fixed budget, not from the incumbent's tuning
history: what signal in the data does the current objective never use (tissue / cell structure, the slide a tile
comes from, its neighbours, its magnification, stain physics), which samples it never sees or sees too often, which
part of the run is spent on what, what the architecture cannot represent. Read the literature (method details, the
scale it was shown at) and cite it in the claim. Ideas from other fields are welcome. A multi-file implementation
(a new module file, a new data pipeline stage, new config keys) is allowed and expected; you have the moonshot
turn and time budget.



## Init and budgets
- Keeping the current init: its pretrained weights must still load: new modules are heads / auxiliary branches, or residual branches initialised to zero so the parent's function is unchanged at step 0. The init-compat check runs on every model.py / train.py change.
- Changing the init or architecture is an init swap: any non-pathology, non-GenBio source; it must reach the full sample budget within the FLOP cap.
- The training budget is the SAME samples and FLOPs: a structural change reallocates compute, it never adds any.
- One training run must still finish inside the 5 h run limit (smoke it).
- Editable files (the ONLY surface a probe can change): model.py, train.py, aug.py, config.yaml
- LOCKED files (never edited): eval.py
- Protected config keys (never changed; a diff touching one is rejected at intake): eval.seed
- The TRAINING BUDGET is fixed: training longer, more steps / samples / FLOPs / epochs, or a longer schedule is impossible. Only the use of the fixed budget can change.
- Seeds: the seed plan is fixed by the loop; a probe cannot ask for more replicates.
- NO change may use GenBio data or models (GenBio-PathFM embeddings, the GenBio-curated subset /data/nanopath-curated-genbiopathfm): usage restrictions; any reference is rejected disallowed_data.
- Init compatibility (keeping the current init): Architecture changes that break model init (parent weights no longer load, changed shapes/names) score MUCH worse: do not make one unless it stays init-compatible; the harness checks it and rejects failures.
- Init swap: Changing the init itself is open (operator 2026-10-07): another pretrained model or size, another architecture, new model code or a random init. A node with another model.type / checkpoint (model.pretrained_url) than its parent is an INIT SWAP, checked before any GPU instead of the parent-relative init check: it constructs as model.py's ViT(variant=model.type) (probe.py builds and strict-loads it the same way), its load_pretrained runs, its forward is finite (else init_incompatible); no pathology-trained or GenBio checkpoint may initialise or guide it (init_illegal); the smoke's measured FLOPs per sample x train.max_train_samples must stay within the FLOP cap (over_flop_cap, with the projected fraction). The recipe's hyperparameters were set for the current init: variants / a branched plan in finish can retune them beside it.
- NO HYPERPARAMETER-SWEEP SPAM (operator): propose a MECHANISM (new code: loss / objective / data / augmentation / architecture / training procedure). A numbers-only change must be substantiated: a MAJOR move (> 2x, to/from 0, or a categorical / schedule switch, e.g. an LR-schedule truncation fix) with its mechanism stated, or a small move the lever regression or a designed batch backs. An unbacked small tweak is rejected (sweep_only), a backed one whose expected effect is below the screen's detectable effect too (below_noise: minute changes fall to noise), and a near-copy of an existing node's change set (same code, every value within 2x, 2x included: 'the same stack + one small tweak') is rejected (near_dup_config); small sweeps belong to designed batches. Probe briefs name a mechanism or a substantiated MAJOR move, not a small value tweak.
- Every probe brief must be ONE change implementable within the editable files and non-protected keys above. Briefs that name a protected key or ask for more training are dropped mechanically.

## Prediction
ONE overall predicted distribution for the change you build (no per-axis budget rows, no dose knob): the chosen
slate candidate's p_neg / median / p_gap, and hypothesis.predictions.panel with the size you actually believe. The
loop's usual advice to shrink predictions toward the past (tiny) mean does NOT apply here: an honest, bold
prediction that is falsified is useful evidence.

what limits the model, how it searches, what it may not change, and how it spends its GPUs. Some of

## 1. List the assumptions, in five lenses
- measurement: is the panel/axis noise what the loop thinks (per-axis and per-dataset spread below)?
  does a 2-seed screen resolve the effects we look for? is the proxy (the probe panel) valid for the
  real target? are shared controls and the corrected estimates trustworthy?

  (samples or FLOPs)? what fraction of each schedule is reached at the stop -- e.g. a schedule keyed to
  train_flops/max_train_flops only reaches the flop_fraction shown at the sample stop, so its LR /
  WD / EMA end values are never the ones it was designed to reach. What are the final lr/wd/ema?

  which families are exhausted, which never really tried?
- constraints: separate HARD external rules (locked files, protected keys, the training budget, eval
  identity, the seed cap, the Labless gate) from SELF-IMPOSED ones (intake rules, family boundaries,

prompt/review:
BIG REVIEW #{n_review} of task `{task_id}` (trigger: {trigger}; {n_scored} scored trials).

You are the principal investigator. Do not summarise ideas one by one: connect ACROSS
them. Find the shared cause behind many separate results and state it as a meta-hypothesis
with a testable prediction.

Example: "six unrelated regularisers all hurt, and every change that lowered the LR helped
a little -> the model is over-trained for this budget -> TRAIN WEAKER: predict that lower LR,
lower weight decay, shorter warmup or weaker augmentation each raise the panel score."
Each such prediction is a lever direction over {lever_vocab}. Also look for dose effects
(mild helped, strong hurt), per-axis trade-offs, and exhausted versus under-sampled families.

Evidence: the CORRECTED world model is the only source of effect sizes. For a trial, cite its
shrunk utility U (mean±sd), P(U>0) and status from the trial table; a trial with P(U>0) near
0.5 or below has NO demonstrated effect, whatever its raw number says. The raw panel column is
raw, uncorrected, single-seed — do not cite it as an effect (shared controls and seed noise move
it by more than most real effects). For a lever, cite the LEVER TREND tables (effect per +1
step, with se; |mean| < 2 se is only "suggestive"); the computed close explanations give mechanism, not size. Every
number you cite must appear below. Hypothesis E values are bounded likelihood ratios against the
claim's PREDICTED size: E_for tests "effect > 0", E_against tests "effect >= the predicted size",
and one trial moves a meta-hypothesis's E by at most 4x (a trial hypothesis's by 20x). A meta
verdict needs E >= K/alpha, K = the number of meta-hypotheses (one bar for the whole family), so it
takes several concordant trials; most metas stay "testing". A meta's trials are the nodes made from
its own probe briefs, then the nodes whose changed config keys / code identifiers its claim and
probes NAME, and only when neither exists, lever-matched nodes: name the exact keys in your probes.
REFUTED means "smaller than predicted", not "harmful".
Trials sharing a baseline run are positively dependent (corrected for, but do not over-read E);
confirmation e-values use fresh seeds and are exact.

  the uncertainty is).
- findings: short, specific, evidence-citing statements (cite node / hypothesis ids).
- meta_hypotheses: 1-4 cross-idea hypotheses. Each has a claim, a mechanism_tag, a
  family (or "cross"), a lever direction vector over {lever_vocab} (non-zero entries
  only, -1/+1), predicted panel sign (+1/-1) and size, a falsification criterion (phrased against
  the node's MEASURE PARENT or the incumbent -- its OWN increment -- never against root: a child of
